elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either Party, including the Company, to terminate the Agreement, and subsection (a) expressly characterizes the Company's termination pursuant to Section 4.1 as termination for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Agreement requires ninety (90) days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is provided.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either Party to terminate on 90 days' written notice and does not prohibit HDI from terminating during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Company may terminate pursuant to Section 4.1 on ninety (90) days' written notice, and subsection (a) expressly recognizes such termination for convenience.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is the lesser of the revenue-based calculation and amounts payable under Section 3.1 for the three calendar months preceding termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause permits either Party to terminate on 90 days' notice without expressly limiting HDI's termination right to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Either Party, including HDI, must give ninety (90) days' written notice.
